help.certs.body: The right panel shows the available certificates. You can inspect their details, check validity, and use them to sign or authenticate depending on the workflow. If none appears, you can use a P12/PFX for the current session only or explicitly import it into a system or browser store.
help.certs.title: Certificates
help.more.body: For advanced operations you can also use the local web console and the GrxFirma command line.
help.more.title: More information
help.security.body: Always review the site requesting a signature or certificate. Do not approve operations you were not expecting. Use resident mode and web compatibility only when necessary.
help.security.title: Security
help.sign.body: Use the Sign tab to sign one file, several files, or a whole folder. For PDF documents in PAdES format you can enable a visible seal, rotation, QR, metadata, and specific pages or all pages. You can keep selectors open or position the seal without rushing: the connected channel allows up to 30 minutes of inactivity.

help.verify.body: In Verify you can validate signed documents and review format, signers, reason, and technical details. After signing, the application automatically verifies the result.
help.verify.title: Verify signatures
help.web.body: The local REST API and web compatibility let GrxFirma integrate with portals and the local web console. Keep these services restricted to the local machine.
help.web.title: Local web integration

help.updates.body: In Settings you can enable or disable the automatic notice. At startup, GrxFirma checks the latest GitHub Release once over HTTPS; it sends no documents, certificates, or signature data and never downloads or runs installers. You can also use About > Check for updates. If the check fails, review the Internet connection or proxy and try again; local signing remains available.
